clue.text: Trendy expert attending a conference in Africa

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable
a dab hand is an expert, so a dab is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashionable specialist turns up at a meeting somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: An INDABA is a tribal gathering among southern African peoples, now used for any important conference.
explanation.definitionFit: Indaba is a Zulu and Xhosa word for a council or consultative meeting of leaders.

clue.text: Face changing sides? Sick about that - it's a slippery slope

indicators.note: the two halves of that word swap places, left going right and right going left
about means around, so the word for sick wraps the other piece

blocks.note: first letter of ILL, meaning unwell
taken as written
rest of ILL, meaning unwell

explanation.surface: A climber swaps one cliff face for another and feels queasy on the steep, slick slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides' swaps the word's two halves, left pair to the right; 'Face' is not a cliff face here.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is a steep, broken section of glacier, literally a frozen slope down which ice moves.

clue.text: Was resident being rude turning up temperature?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: rude in the sense of smutty
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A lodger behaving badly turns the heating up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to live somewhere, so it means lived or resided.

clue.text: Clear space and test out long piece of needlework

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a blank is an empty space
taken as written
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Clear a space and try out a lengthy sewing project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a description of the needlework, but it is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket stitch is a decorative buttonhole-style stitch worked along the edge of fabric, originally for blankets.

clue.text: Keep mum quiet? That's debatable on reflection!

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the adjective in the idiom 'keep shtoom'

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so that word is read backwards

blocks.note: the hushing sound asking for quiet
a moot point is one open to debate

explanation.surface: Someone tells a mother to stay silent, then wonders whether that is even arguable.
explanation.walkthrough: SHTOOM (also shtum) is Yiddish-derived slang for silent; 'keep shtoom' means say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay silent, and shtoom is a slang adjective for silent used in exactly that phrase.

clue.text: Poor actor having real trouble in Dutch venue

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so those letters are disordered

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad actor has genuine difficulties performing at a theatre in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Haarlem is a Dutch city near Amsterdam, a place where events happen, hence a venue.

clue.text: They're in deep, taking month over English version of opera)

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
in a down clue, the month sits over the next piece
opera is the Latin plural of opus; the English plural adds -es

explanation.surface: Something about an operatic production translated into English, staged during one month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera' looks like musical theatre, but it is the plural of opus, a work. The deep is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopuses are sea creatures, and 'the deep' is a poetic name for the ocean, so they live in it.

clue.text: Type of handicraft club adopting computer facility

indicators.note: a family adopting someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a mace is a heavy war club
RAM is a computer's random-access memory

explanation.surface: A crafts society takes on a new computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The published grid prints MECRAME in its unchecked second cell, a slip; the wordplay and the craft give MACRAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is the craft of knotting cord or string into decorative patterns.

clue.text: Particularly thin boxes, extremely fragile

indicators.note: at the extreme end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a boxer spars in practice
the last letter of fragile

explanation.surface: A delicate cardboard carton, especially flimsy at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun for containers, but it is the verb, as a boxer spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, as with sparse hair or sparse population.

clue.text: Usual procedure for dealing with complaints?

blocks.note: first meaning: the normal way things are done, in general
second meaning: a family doctor's surgery, where illnesses are treated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' suggests grievances to be handled, but here they are ailments; a GP (general practitioner) is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means common custom, and is also the branch of medicine a family doctor practises when treating ailments.

clue.text: Exclude number of Mozart's works to put in another composer

indicators.note: something put in goes inside the pieces around it

blocks.note: to bar is to shut out
taken as written
Mozart's works are numbered in the Köchel catalogue, cited as K

explanation.surface: A music cataloguer drops one of Mozart's pieces and slips in a different composer instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number of Mozart's works' points to the Köchel catalogue, whose numbers are prefixed K; Bartók was Hungarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer, and the clue has already mentioned Mozart, hence another one.

clue.text: Dramatic representation of year with poll involved

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
joins the two words of fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A play dramatises a year in which an election took centre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is acting out a part, a kind of dramatic representation used in training and therapy.

clue.text: Formal dress what's needed - I bet casual is out

definitions.text: Formal dress what's needed - I bet casual is out

blocks.note: surface reading: a guest wondering what to wear to a smart event
setter's reading: the dress code printed on an invitation, which rules out casual clothes

explanation.surface: A guest guesses that a smart event demands formal wear and jeans won't do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I bet casual' looks like anagram fodder, but its letters do not fit; the clue simply describes the dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: Black tie is the dress-code term for a dinner jacket and bow tie, the standard formal evening wear.

clue.text: Race up and act friskily

indicators.note: moving friskily is jumping about playfully, so the letters skip into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
joins the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dash up and play about like a lively young animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a caper is to leap or dance about playfully, a caper being a skipping jump.

clue.text: Main source of accommodation for retired people

definitions.text: Main source of accommodation for retired people

blocks.clueFragment: Main source of accommodation for retired people
blocks.note: surface reading: the chief provider of housing for pensioners, like a care home
setter's reading: people who have retired for the night, gone to bed, and the main room in a house where they sleep

explanation.surface: Who chiefly provides homes for people living on their pensions?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: The master bedroom is the principal bedroom of a house, where its owners sleep after retiring for the night.

clue.text: See 3
Go into decline as a result of dock strike?

definitions.text: as a result of dock strike?

blocks.note: first meaning: dwindle or fade away

blocks.clueFragment: as a result of dock strike?
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: docking an animal cuts its tail, so the tail is then gone

explanation.walkthrough: A dock strike sounds like a walkout by port workers, but to dock is to cut short an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail off is to diminish gradually, and a docked dog has literally had its tail removed.

clue.text: American source of extraterrestrial transmissions

blocks.note: surface reading: somewhere in America picking up signals from aliens
setter's reading: radio messages to and from astronauts in space, handled by NASA mission control in a Texas city

explanation.surface: Where in the USA do messages from outer space come from?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraterrestrial' suggests aliens, but it means messages beyond Earth, as in 'Houston, we have a problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan city hosts NASA's Mission Control Center, which talks to crews in space.

clue.text: A US president joins king wearing graduate scarf

indicators.note: whatever is wearing something has it wrapped around the outside

blocks.note: first part of BA, a Bachelor of Arts
taken as written
either President Bush
K is the chess abbreviation for king
second part of BA, a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A president and a monarch meet, the latter dressed in a university scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: A + BUSH + K sits inside BA, the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A babushka is a headscarf tied under the chin, named after the Russian word for grandmother who wears one.

clue.text: Serious conflict caused by temper - time left to intervene?

indicators.note: whatever intervenes comes between, so it goes into the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: a bate is British slang for a fit of temper
T is the abbreviation for time
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A grave quarrel sparked by bad temper, with a pause needed to calm things down.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'in a bate' is old British schoolboy slang for being in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a large-scale fight between armies, a serious conflict.

clue.text: See 14
One's likely to hover over half-demolished street in part of Hull

indicators.note: half of the building is knocked down, so only half its letters stay
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the keel runs along the bottom of a ship's hull
the first half of street

explanation.surface: Something hovers over a wrecked road in the English city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire port city, but it is a ship's hull. The kestrel is famous for hovering while hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon known for hovering in place while watching the ground for prey.

clue.text: Sixes are significant - one seen at Lord's?

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals, and VIs is the plural
things that count matter

explanation.surface: At the cricket, big hits for six matter a lot to someone watching at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, where sixes are big hits; here it means the House of Lords, where peers sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a peer ranking below an earl, entitled to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Three consecutive letters with purpose to reduce tension?

blocks.note: D, E and F follow one another in the alphabet
joins the two pieces
the use of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's question: can three letters in a row with a purpose calm things down?
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a situation is to calm it, as a bomb disposal expert removes the fuse that would make it explode.

clue.text: Someone demanding penalty is not so thick

blocks.note: first meaning: one who fines
second meaning: comparative of fine, slender

explanation.surface: The person insisting on punishment is not as stupid as you'd think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' suggests stupid, but here it means wide, the opposite of fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A finer imposes fines, and finer is also the comparative of fine meaning thin or slender.

clue.text: Angles straightened out in nurse's bedside manner

definitions.text: Angles straightened out in nurse's bedside manner

blocks.clueFragment: Angles straightened out in nurse's bedside manner
blocks.note: surface reading: a nurse's tactful way with patients sorting out awkward matters
setter's reading: the way a nurse literally makes a bed, folding the sheet ends into neat tucked angles

explanation.surface: A nurse's tact with patients smooths out tricky angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angles straightened out' looks like an anagram of ANGLES, but no letters are shuffled; 'bedside manner' is taken literally as a way of making a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital corners are tight diagonal folds at the foot of a bed sheet, the way nurses are taught to tuck it.

clue.text: In favour of international European currency

blocks.note: to be for something is to favour it
INT is the standard short form

explanation.surface: Someone backs a currency that crosses borders across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the monetary unit of Hungary, a European country outside the euro.

clue.text: Behaving unethically in morning exam

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for an adjective describing such conduct

blocks.note: a.m. is short for ante meridiem, before noon
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student caught cheating during a test held before lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amoral lacks any moral sense and so conducts themselves without regard for right and wrong.
